rules.statement: Never treat an unsupported or unmatched `ui_locales` preference as an error: an authorization or end-session request's validation must not check `ui_locales` against `ui_locales_supported`, and a preference that matches nothing just falls back to another locale.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §3.1.2.1 says an unsupported locale SHOULD NOT cause an error. A preference the provider can't meet is one the end-user simply doesn't get.
rules.check: Look for request validators or handlers that reject, log an error for, or return an OAuth error when a `ui_locales` value is missing from the supported set.

rules.statement: A `*_supported` setting that discovery advertises, such as `ui_locales_supported`, must accept only values from a registered vocabulary of things the server actually implements or renders, and options validation must reject unregistered values.
rules.why: A free-form list would advertise locales or features nothing renders, and a request for one would silently get something else. A registered vocabulary keeps the advertisement true.
rules.check: Look for new or changed discoverable supported-values settings whose descriptor or validator accepts any well-formed string without checking it against the registered catalog.

rules.statement: When selecting a UI locale, match each preference in order using RFC 4647 §3.4 lookup (the full tag, then the tag with its last subtag removed), case-insensitively, and apply the tenant's supported-locales ceiling to the fallback default as well as to the preferences, so that a configured default outside the ceiling is never rendered.
rules.why: If the ceiling bounds the fallback the same way it bounds a preference, a page always renders in a locale that discovery advertises, and the advertised set never disagrees with the rendered default.
rules.check: Look at locale-selection code for exact-match-only comparisons, case-sensitive tag matching, or a fallback to a default or first locale that skips the supported-locales ceiling.

rules.statement: When parsing `Accept-Language` into locale preferences, order the entries by descending quality and drop the `*` wildcard and any entry with a quality of zero.
rules.why: The user agent's preferences have to be read in their stated priority, and q=0 or the wildcard names no language to render.
rules.check: Look for `Accept-Language` parsing that keeps header order regardless of q-values, or that passes `*` or q=0 entries on as preferences.

rules.statement: Carry the end-user's `ui_locales` preference across interactive pages on the redirect URL's `ui_locales` query and as a hidden `ui_locales` form field. Don't look up the parked authorization request on each page, and don't store the locale in a cookie.
rules.why: A store read keyed by a query value on every anonymous request is a cost any caller can impose. A cookie is extra state the tenant route must scope and a second source of truth. The query and the hidden field carry the choice exactly as far as it applies, at no cost.
rules.check: Look for login, consent or logout pages that load stored request state, or set or read a cookie, to work out the UI language, and for redirects or forms between interactive pages that drop the `ui_locales` value.

rules.statement: Server-rendered pages must write the selected locale's tag into the `lang` attribute of the `html` element, and client-side code must render in that page language instead of negotiating its own language from `navigator.languages`.
rules.why: If the client negotiated on its own, the no-JavaScript pages would stay in one language, the first frame would flash another, and the document's `lang` would not match what the user reads.
rules.check: Look for rendered HTML documents without a server-set `lang`, or front-end code that picks its locale from `navigator.language(s)` rather than the document's `lang`.

rules.statement: When several DI registration methods contribute to an ordered collection whose order decides a default, make each method end by putting the registrations into a canonical order that depends only on the set of registered items, never on the order in which the methods were called.
rules.why: An order that depends on the calls makes the default a property of the host's composition order. Nothing documents that, and reordering `Program.cs` would change it without a test failing.
rules.check: Look for extension methods that append to a shared enumerable registration where the first registration becomes the default and the result depends on which `Add*` call ran first.

rules.statement: Don't rely on `TryAddEnumerable` to dedupe or replace data registered as singleton instances that share one implementation type. Find and replace the existing instance by its identifying key (for example, a tag or name) instead.
rules.why: `TryAddEnumerable` dedupes by implementation type, so it can't tell apart instances of the same record type that carry different data.
rules.check: Look for `TryAddEnumerable` calls that register instances of a record or data type expected to be unique per key rather than per type.

rules.statement: Validate at host startup, with an options validator, that every registered strategy or data item a component depends on is of the kind that component can use (for example, a UI locale that carries the messages the pages need), and also refuse an incompatible registration at the point of use.
rules.why: The error is then found at deploy time, never by an end-user, and no page renders text in one language under the tag of another.
rules.check: Look for consumers that silently skip, cast unsafely, or fall back when a registered item lacks what they need, with no startup validator that stops the host.

rules.statement: Localize host-extensible server-rendered text with registered message records that a host can add or adapt through DI, not with `.resx` satellite-assembly resources.
rules.why: Satellite assemblies are closed to a host that wants to add a language or change wording, while a small registered message record can be replaced or extended.
rules.check: Look for new `.resx` files or `IStringLocalizer` resource lookups introduced for extensible end-user interface text.
